about.title: Modesto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Stanislaus County's largest city moves a lot of traffic through a fairly compact grid, and the public record shows what that looks like. In 2025, Modesto logged 1,365 injury collisions, with 1,992 people hurt and 20 lives lost. Coffee Road, Oakdale Road, Tully Road and Briggsmore Avenue appear most often in those reports, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for a noticeable share of them. If one of those numbers now describes your week, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. Adjusters call quickly. Repair estimates, medical bills and time away from work start stacking up. We handle car accident claims in Modesto. Our service is free, and we work on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we take it from there.

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California allows two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. An early call keeps those dates from sneaking up.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your share of fault simply reduces the amount. We can push back when an adjuster tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Protecting your evidence and your words
items.desc: The other driver's insurer will likely ask for a recorded statement, and you are not required to give one. We work on contingency and can step in to preserve photos, dashcam footage and repair records before they disappear.

items.question: I was hit on Briggsmore Avenue during Friday rush hour. What should I do first?
items.answer: Get checked by a doctor even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back symptoms often show up a day or two later. Photograph the vehicles, the intersection and any signal or lane markings before the scene clears, and request the Modesto Police or CHP report number. Then contact us, and we can help you take over communication with the insurers.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are under no legal obligation to give a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can later be used to reduce or deny your claim. Keep your own insurer informed as your policy requires, but let us handle the other side.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases. What you may actually recover depends on the facts, the available insurance and any fault assigned to you under comparative negligence. We can explain how those factors apply to your specific Modesto crash.
